clue.text: Enters the race-late starter in it — and finishes

indicators.note: the late starter goes inside the word just built, so 'in it' marks the container

parts.note: to enter a race is to compete, so this gives competes

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter, here of 'late'

explanation.surface: A runner who joined the race late still manages to cross the finishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' picks L from 'late', and 'in it' puts that L inside COMPETES.
explanation.definitionFit: To complete a job is to bring it to an end, a plain synonym of finish.

clue.text: About to leave, the English pay back in kind

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word for about or concerning
to quit a place is to leave it

explanation.surface: The English, about to depart, decide to return a favour in kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To requite is to repay or return like for like, whether kindness or injury.

clue.text: Pressed down, if print for example is needed

definitions.text: Pressed down, if print for example is needed

indicators.note: letters squashed and pressed into a new shape are being rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone taking fingerprints presses down on the pad whenever a print is wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of IFPRINT with EG gives the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: it is what you press down when a print is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a fingerprint means pressing the end of a finger on to ink and then paper.

clue.text: Encourage head boy at one point to tear out a whisker

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of 'boy'

parts.note: E (east) is one point of the compass

indicators.note: letters thrown out of order are rearranged, so 'out' signals the anagram

explanation.surface: Egging on the head boy to rip out one of his whiskers at some point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TEAR into ATER. 'whisker' is not facial hair but a thing that whisks, a kitchen tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisk for beating eggs is literally something that whisks, so a whisker in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: She advises linking lowa to Hungarian city

parts.note: Eger is a city in northern Hungary
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: An adviser arranges a twinning of a town in Iowa with a Hungarian city.
explanation.walkthrough: Egeria was the nymph who counselled King Numa of Rome, so her name now means a woman adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend Egeria counselled King Numa, and her name is used for any female counsellor.

clue.text: Beds laid out include socially acceptable shrub

indicators.note: the anagram takes in the next piece, so 'include' marks the container
laid out of order, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder as the setter meant it, the words bed and laid, singular bed
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Flower beds have been planted out to take in a respectable shrub.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints 'Beds', but the answer has no S, so the fodder should read 'Bed'. U for upper-class, 'socially acceptable', is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Buddleia is a flowering bush often called the butterfly bush.

clue.text: Makes a connection with a girl, pert perhaps

definitions.note: the clue's phrase stands for a thing that makes a connection, a noun

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: 'perhaps' says the letters given could be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A man makes a connection with a girl, perhaps a cheeky one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges PERT into PTER. The definition is read as 'one that makes a connection'.
explanation.definitionFit: An adapter is a fitting that joins two devices or plugs not otherwise compatible.

clue.text: Points many do not win, yet fence effectively

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
C is the Roman numeral 100, standing for many
to lose is not to win

explanation.surface: A fencer scores many points without winning, yet still fences well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' is not the sport but to put a fence round something.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a barrier all round an area is in effect to fence it in.

clue.text: Former student observing instructions

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
eying something is observing it

explanation.surface: An old boy of the school is still watching out for instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The old boy watching instructions is doing what the answer says, so the whole clue serves as definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Following orders as given is complying with them.

clue.text: Promote a loan

definitions.meaning: to promote someone is to move them up in rank
money paid ahead of time, such as against wages

explanation.definitionFit: To advance someone is to promote them, and an advance is money lent ahead of time.

clue.text: Diver goes through holding breathing apparatus

indicators.note: the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: per means through or by means of
a lung is the organ we breathe with

explanation.surface: A diver passes through the water with breathing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breathing apparatus' looks like scuba gear but is the body's own lung.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plunges into water is a diver, so a plunger in the literal sense.

clue.text: Nail is too twisted for withdrawal

indicators.note: twisted out of shape, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A nail is too bent to be pulled out.
explanation.definitionFit: Withdrawal from company leaves one alone, cut off from others.

clue.text: Record-holders

parts.note: read not as champions but as things holding vinyl records

explanation.definitionFit: Paper or card covers protect vinyl discs, holding the records.

clue.text: About ten relax outside

indicators.note: turned about, the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Around ten o'clock it's time to relax outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a container or the RE for 'about', but here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: External describes what lies on the outer side, a synonym of outside.

clue.text: Serial recast, based in the Middle East

definitions.note: describes a country located in that region

indicators.note: a serial recast has its cast changed, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A TV serial gets a new cast and is now set in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: The country lies on the eastern Mediterranean coast, within the region of southwest Asia.

clue.text: Slips in calculation due to using this?

definitions.text: Slips in calculation due to using this?

parts.words: Slips in calculation due to using this?
parts.note: plays on a sliding rule-based calculating tool, one whose parts slip along each other

explanation.definitionFit: This instrument calculates by moving one graduated scale along another.

clue.text: Never fails —- nameless remedy for warding off death

indicators.note: to remedy is to put right, so the letters are reordered
N is the abbreviation for name, which is dropped

explanation.surface: A cure that never fails has kept someone from death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' drops the N from NEVER FAILS, and 'remedy' rearranges EVERFAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer or rescue device saves people from dying.

clue.text: Sick English convict set loose? it's against regulations!

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: loosened, the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: lag is slang for a convict

explanation.surface: Freeing an ailing English prisoner breaks the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set loose' rearranges LAG into GAL. Lag (an old lag) is British slang for a long-serving prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking a rule or law makes an act unlawful.

clue.text: Arsonists aboard them?

parts.note: people who start fires are fire-starters, and the same word names flat barges used to unload ships

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both people who set things alight and flat-bottomed barges.

clue.text: On first of September, parking beyond river, I fish

indicators.note: the parking letter comes after the river
the first letter of 'September' is taken

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: On the first of September I parked by the river to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Scampi are langoustine tails, sold as seafood, hence 'fish' in a loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Scampi are breaded shellfish tails served in British pubs as a fish dish.

clue.text: Means of conveyance of goods — and germs

definitions.text: Means of conveyance of goods — and germs

parts.words: Means of conveyance of goods — and germs
parts.note: one word covers a haulage firm moving goods and a person who passes on infection

explanation.definitionFit: A haulier moves goods, and someone passing on a disease without symptoms is said to transmit it.

clue.text: Superior accommodation for person with one child about one

parts.note: man means a person

indicators.note: the child goes around the second one

parts.note: a son is one child
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A grand home for a man with a single child.
explanation.definitionFit: A large grand house is the most luxurious kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Female swan circling river at Stourhead settles on temporary resting-place

indicators.note: going round, the first letter is carried to the far end

parts.note: a pen is a female swan
the Cam is the river in Cambridge
read as Stour head, the first letter of Stour

explanation.surface: A female swan circles the river at the Stourhead estate before settling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' moves the P of PENCAM round to the end, giving ENCAMP. 'at' is a link word. Stourhead is a famous English landscape garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To camp is to settle temporarily in tents or shelter.

clue.text: Show newsman returning inside with proof

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to evince is to show or display

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a newsman

explanation.surface: Show the reporter coming back with the proof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the editor round to DE. 'Show' looks like a noun, but it is the verb evince.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is what establishes facts, such as proof in court.

clue.text: Grass-moth seen to swerve around in one direction

indicators.note: the swerve goes around the direction

parts.note: to veer is to swerve
NE, northeast, is one compass direction

explanation.surface: A grass moth is seen to swerve around in one direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Veneer moths are a group of small moths found in grassland.

clue.text: Country restricting his right to vote

indicators.note: the country holds the next word inside it

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A country limits his voting rights.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the vote, the citizen's suffrage.

clue.text: A blessed blow-out, with van caught in rain storm

indicators.note: the van is trapped inside the other piece
in a storm, the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A van broke down in a rainstorm, a blessed relief to the passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' rearranges the rain into NIRA. The Sanskrit word literally means a blowing out, as of a flame.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this state of bliss is the extinguishing of desire, a blessed snuffing out.

clue.text: But are such companies incapable of expansion?

definitions.text: But are such companies incapable of expansion?

parts.words: But are such companies incapable of expansion?
parts.note: plays on the 'Ltd' type of firm, whose name sounds as if it is capped in size

explanation.definitionFit: A company with liability restricted to its shares carries a word meaning restricted.

clue.text: Sell pie? That's bad form!

indicators.note: bad means the letters are spoiled into another order

explanation.surface: Trying to sell pie is bad manners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like manners but is a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipse is an oval shape, a geometric figure.

clue.text: Plays the joker when partner's king is in trouble

definitions.note: stands for a person who plays the joker, a noun

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disorder

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: In bridge a player fools around when partner's king is in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in trouble' rearranges PARTNERS and K together.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical joker plays tricks on others, playing the fool.
